claim: The Reassessing Extractive QA study reports that LLM-as-a-judge performs particularly well on number-related answers but faces challenges with more complex types, such as job titles.
quote: Further analysis reveals that LLM-as-a-judge performs particularly well on number-related answers but faces challenges with more complex types, such as job titles.

claim: The same study reports that zero-shot, context-free judging often yields the best evaluation performance.
quote: Finally, we find that prompt phrasing has minimal impact, and zero-shot, context-free judging often yields the best evaluation performance.

claim: The graph-verified financial-documents study reports that a grounded judge, given the full source document but no ground truth, achieved only 54.3% agreement, with a 33.1% false acceptance rate.
quote: A grounded judge-given the full source document but no ground truthachieves only 54.3% agreement, with a 33.1% false acceptance rate-approving 1 in 3 wrong answers even with the source material in context.

claim: In the graph-verified financial-documents study, a lenient judge inflates disagreement with the verified truth to 7.9%, and a blind judge without ground truth reaches 22.3%.
quote: A lenient judge inflates this to 7.9% and a blind judge (without ground truth) reaches 22.3%.

claim: The authors report that false acceptances concentrate in exact recall, multi-hop and threshold categories.
quote: False acceptances concentrate in exact recall (50%), multi-hop (46%), and threshold (33%) categories-precisely the structured tasks where accuracy matters most in financial regulation.

claim: The authors of the Quebec insurance legal-QA judging study conclude that a single LLM judge is not trustworthy enough to evaluate high-stakes legal answers on its own.
quote: We conclude that a single LLM judge is not trustworthy enough to evaluate high-stakes legal answers on its own, and argue for cost-aware, human-in-the-loop use in deployment.

claim: The Quebec insurance legal-QA judging study reports that selecting judges by their ability to catch errors, supplying an authoritative reference, and combining a few strong judges each reduces dangerous acceptances.
quote: Selecting judges by their ability to catch errors, supplying an authoritative reference, and combining a few strong judges each reduces these dangerous acceptances.

claim: The SCITAB authors report that all models except GPT-4 achieved performance barely above random guessing on table-based scientific claims.
quote: All models except GPT-4 achieved performance barely above random guessing.

claim: The SCITAB authors also report that popular prompting techniques such as Chain-of-Thought do not achieve much performance gains on SCITAB.
quote: Popular prompting techniques, such as Chain-of-Thought, do not achieve much performance gains on SCITAB.

claim: In an error analysis of program-of-thought predictions, the SCITAB authors categorized failures as grounding, ambiguity, calculation and program errors.
quote: We divide the errors into four categories, as assessed by human annotators: (i) Grounding errors, where the program incorrectly associates data with the respective cells in the table ; (ii) Ambiguity errors, where the claim contains ambiguous expressions that the program fails to represent; (iii) Calculation errors, where incorrect floating point arithmetic calculation in Python lead to inaccurate results and (iv) Program errors, which encompass mistakes such as incorrect or missing arguments/variables, and erroneous operations.

claim: The ClaimDB authors argue that at large scale, approaches that rely on reading the evidence break down, forcing a shift toward reasoning in executable programs.
quote: At this scale, verification approaches that rely on "reading" the evidence break down, forcing a timely shift toward reasoning in executable programs.

claim: The Prolog study notes that chain-of-thought relies on an LLM to generate a sequence of arithmetic calculations which can be prone to cascaded calculation errors.
quote: However, the CoT approach relies on an LLM to generate a sequence of arithmetic calculations which can be prone to cascaded calculation errors.

claim: The MT-Bench authors present methods to address position bias and the limited grading ability for math questions.
quote: We present a few methods to address position bias and the limited grading ability for math questions.

claim: The construct-validity study reports that high judge agreement can coexist with weak sensitivity to changes in the construct being evaluated.
quote: These results show that high judge agreement can coexist with weak sensitivity to changes in the construct being evaluated, motivating joint reporting of invariance and sensitivity and auditing the validation set itself.

claim: The Survey on LLM-as-a-Judge says future work should fuse LLM judges with symbolic solvers or knowledge bases and build judges able to interpret figures and tables.
quote: Future work should fuse LLM judges with symbolic solvers or medical knowledge bases for fact-checking, incorporate uncertainty estimation (e.g. calibrated refusals), and design multimodal-aware judges capable of interpreting figures and tables.
